subject: Region tethering and legal-hold interaction — acceptance criteria & exportability
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintrust.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Aiden Cho <aiden@cloudops.fintrust.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify: legal-hold vs. region tethering for Dedicated deployment

Hi Ben —

Thanks for taking this. FinTrust is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for EU-only processing but our legal team has flagged an edge case: when a litigation hold (legal hold) is placed, we must preserve and be able to export all tenant data and associated metadata without cross-border movement. Questions:

- If we pin a tenant to the Frankfurt region, can snapshots, backups, or disaster-recovery copies ever leave the EU for any reason (automated replication, temporary evacuation, vendor backups)?
- Is it possible to produce an in-region export that includes ephemeral KV caches and the full snapshot chain required for eDiscovery without pulling data into another region?
- What evidence/artifacts can you provide for chain-of-custody and for the timing of any data movement?

Attached is a short note from our legal ops (fintrust-legal-hold-requirements.pdf). Can you confirm next steps and an acceptance criteria list we can take to compliance?

Regards,
Elena Morales
Head of Legal Ops — FinTrust

Attachments: fintrust-legal-hold-requirements.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintrust.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify: legal-hold vs. region tethering for Dedicated deployment

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the doc. Looping in Kimberly (infra/privacy), Rishi (product/compliance), and Soojin (ops).

Quick read: we can meet these requirements but need to align on a few operational constraints. Proposed next steps:

1) Kimberly to sketch what stays in-region vs. infra-only artifacts that may replicate.
2) We’ll produce a draft acceptance criteria checklist + runbook (runbook-region-tethering-draft.md) that includes export steps and logs we can hand over.
3) Schedule a working session with FinTrust legal + our ops to agree the export format and turnaround SLAs.

Kimberly/Rishi/Soojin — can you review the attached runbook and add any evidence artifacts you think compliance will need?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintrust.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-25T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: legal-hold vs. region tethering for Dedicated deployment

Elena / team — some technical clarifications from infra:

- Tenant pinning: compute, live model state, and tenant-scoped object storage can be pinned to a specific region (e.g., eu-central-1).
- Snapshots & backups: by default, we keep primary snapshots in-region. For DR we may maintain cross-region replicas only if the customer opts into multi-region DR. For Dedicated EU pinning we can disable cross-region snapshot replication.
- Ephemeral KV / caches: cache contents (KV cache, prefix caches) are in-memory on region-bound nodes; they are not replicated across regions. However, cache contents may appear in ephemeral snapshots if configured — we will ensure those are excluded for legal-hold exports unless explicitly requested.
- Metadata & chain-of-custody: we can provide append-only audit logs (SHA256 hashes + timestamps) for snapshot creation, retention tags, and any administrative export actions.

Draft acceptance criteria (proposal):
- No automatic cross-region snapshot replication for tenant data (explicit opt-in only).
- Exports for legal-hold return: full in-region snapshot chain, KV cache dump (if requested), and a signed audit log of related actions (timestamps + operator IDs).
- Exports are delivered as a downloadable archive stored in customer-controlled, in-region object storage for a configurable retention window.
- Signed attestation that no data transfer occurred outside the EU during the preservation window.

Artifacts we can produce: snapshot manifest (JSON), signed audit log (CSV + SHA256), boot-id and node mapping for the snapshot chain, and ephemeral cache dump (optional). I’ll add these to the runbook doc.

—Kimberly
Infra Privacy Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@fintrust.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Aiden Cho <aiden@cloudops.fintrust.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-25T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: legal-hold vs. region tethering for Dedicated deployment

Thanks Kimberly — that helps. A few follow-ups from legal:

- For eDiscovery we will need the full snapshot chain to be exportable as an artifact with a verifiable chain-of-custody (hashes & timestamps). If you exclude caches by default, can you include an option to export the caches as part of the legal-hold package so we have a forensics snapshot?
- We need a statement about emergency evacuations: if Redwood triggers a cross-region evacuation (for hardware incident or outage), what are the triggers, what approvals are required, and can you ensure preserved copies remain in-region until legal releases the hold?
- Can you provide sample artifacts (manifest + signed log) from an internal test run so our team can validate format?

If you can provide a short acceptance checklist and sample artifacts by Monday, we can move an internal review faster.

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: Clarify: legal-hold vs. region tethering for Dedicated deployment

Elena — following up with an operational proposal and deliverables list. We want to be explicit so compliance can sign off: 

Operational proposal (summary):
- Region tethering: tenant compute, storage, and live model state remain in EU. Cross-region snapshot replication is disabled for this tenant by default.
- Emergency evacuation: only in two scenarios (1) verified physical compromise of the region, (2) region-wide catastrophic failure preventing in-region recovery within agreed RTO. Evacuation requires approval from Redwood security + customer SOC rep (DocuSign acknowledgment). Evacuated copies will remain read-only and flagged; we will retain a verifiable audit trail and we will not delete preserved copies until legal release.

Deliverables we will produce for FinTrust: 
- Acceptance checklist (one-page) describing the in-region constraints and export steps.
- Sample artifact bundle from an internal test: snapshot-manifest.json, signed-audit-log.csv, cache-dump.bin (if requested).
- Chain-of-custody attestation letter (signed PDF).
- Runbook excerpt with RACI and SLAs for legal-hold exports.

Timeline: sample artifacts + checklist by 2028-07-30. If acceptable, we’ll schedule a live export run with FinTrust on 2028-08-03.

Attachments: proposed-sla-amendment-summary.pdf (draft)

—Rishi
Product Compliance — Redwood Inference
